answer: In PoA, each bonded identity escrows capital, and evidence of coordinated equivocation triggers penalties across the implicated set: k identities create up to k(k−1)/2 culpable pairs, so aggregate losses scale as O(k²). Because correlated failures also raise the protocol’s detection multiplier, a sybil swarm can suffer exponential capital loss rather than gain safety by splitting stake. The walnut, relic, and hollow labels do not alter this shared-risk accounting.
